content.text:
I appreciate your detailed request, but I must inform you that **the provided document does not contain information about operative rental housing obligations and exemptions across the categories you've specified**.

The document is a Los Angeles City Council motion from September 3, 2024, that focuses specifically on algorithmic pricing for rent-setting. It does not address:

- Rent caps (status, dates, sanctions, coverage)
- Just cause eviction (status, dates, sanctions, coverage)
- Deposits (status, dates, sanctions, coverage)
- Application/screening fees (status, dates, sanctions, coverage)
- Screening restrictions (status, dates, sanctions, coverage)

Regarding **algorithmic pricing specifically**, the document only discusses:

citations.cited_text:
SOURCE: https://cityclerk.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2024/24-1031_misc_9-03-24.pdf
RETRIEVED: 2026-10-01 22:36 UTC

MOTION
SEP 0 3 2024
I THEREFORE MOVE that the City Council instruct the Los Angeles Housing Department to 
report on the number of ownership and management entities that are using algorithm-based 
software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on the use of this software to set 
rents in the City.

content.text: A motion instructing the Los Angeles Housing Department to report on the number of ownership and management entities using algorithm-based software to establish rents and the feasibility of instituting a ban on this software
. This represents a **proposed action** (not yet enacted as of the document date), with

citations.cited_text:
In July 2024, the San Francisco Board of Supervisors approved 
legislation to ban property owners and managers from using algorithm-based tools that recommend 
or set rental prices.

content.text: San Francisco having approved legislation in July 2024 to ban property owners and managers from using algorithm-based tools that recommend or set rental prices

.

To obtain comprehensive information about all operative rental housing obligations and exemptions as of October 1, 2026, you would need to consult Los Angeles municipal code, Housing Department regulations, and subsequent legislative enactments beyond this single motion document.
